ओवरले तकनबक का उपयोर् करक े  भूस्खलन संवेदनशबलता मानवित्र तैयार करना है और इस क्षेत्र को भूस्खलन प्रवण क्षेत्रों की
वववभन्न वडग्रब में वर्ीक ृत करना है। यह भूस्खलन सूिब डेटाीेस तैयार करक े और उच्च ररज़ॉल्यूशन ररमोट सेंससंर् तकनबकों और फील्ड
इनपुट का उपयोर् कर प्रासंवर्क भौर्ोवलक -कारकों या ववषयर्त मानवित्रों क े वलए टॉपोशबट-वार स्थावनक डेटाीेस तैयार करक े
हावसल ककया जाता है। ववश्लेषणात्मक पदानुक्रम प्रकक्रया कारक वर्ों की पारस्पररक जो़िब-तुलना तुलना क े वलए वनयोवजत है। कारक
वर्ों क े वलए रेटटंर् को क्षेत्रबय ज्ञान क े माध्यम से उद्देश्य ज्ञान, ििाग और पुनः मूल्यांकन क े आिार पर असाइन ककया र्या है। क ुल िह
भौर्ोवलक कारक जैसे ढलान कोण , वक्रता, भूवम उप योर् और भूवम कवर (एलयूएलसब), जोमोफोलॉजब, ढलान ीनाने सामग्रब
(एसएफएम) और रेर्ोवलथ मोटाई नक्शे इनपुट ववषयर्त नक्शे क े  रूप में इस्तेमाल ककया र्या था। नक्शे को संवेदनशबलता स्कोर मैप
प्राप्त करने क े  वलए भाररत मल्टबक्लास इंडेक्स ओवरले वववि का उपयोर् करक े  जबआईएस में एकीक ृ त ककया र्या था, वजसे आवखरकार
कारक वर्ों की समग्र रेटटंर् वर्ीक ृत करक े  प्राप्त ककए र्ए ब्रेक वैल्यू क े  आिार पर 'उच्च', 'मध्यम' और 'कम' में वर्ीक ृत ककया र्या था।
भूस्खलन क े साथ अपने स्थावनक संींि क े  संींि में।
क ु ल वमलाकर 25 भूस्खलन दस्तावेज ककए र्ए हैं, वजनमें से 22 मलीे स्लाइड्स हैं, 3 रॉक स्लाइड और 1 मृदा  फ्लो  हैं। इसक े अलावा,
र्ूर्ल एअथगइमेजरब क े माध्यम से लर्भर् 27 प्राक ृ वतक भूस्खलन की पहिान की र्ई। मौजूदा भूस्खलन क े  फील्ड अवलोकन और
दस्तावेज़बकरण से पता िलता है कक मानसून क े मौसम में ीाररश से वे ी़िे पैमाने पर रिर्र होते हैं। इसक े अलावा, ढलान प्रोफाइल में
संशोिन क े माध्यम से महत्वपूणग मानववंशबय हस्तक्षेप स्थानबय अवस्थरता को प्रेररत करने क े वलए एक प्रमुख कारक कारक पाया र्या
है। अध्ययन में वविार ककए र्ए िह भौर्ोवलक कारकों में से , ढलान और एलयूएलसब क्रमशः 13 और 9 का पूणाांक भार लेते हैं और
भूस्खलन क े  स्थावनक ववतरण में अविकतम वनयंत्रण रखते हैं। ढलान कारक में, 25 वडग्रब -35 वडग्रब कक्षाओं में अविकतम भूस्खलन
घटना फवौरावीवलटब  स्कोर मूल्य है जीकक भूवम उपयोर् और भूवम कवर में , स़िक र्वलयारे क े  साथ व्यापक ढलान कट और खदान
खंड उच्चतम लैंडस्लाइड घटना फवौरावीवलटब  स्कोर मूल्य है। जोमोर्फ ग क कारक वर्ों में, डेनडशनल पहाव़ियों और अत्यविक ववच्िेदन
ढलानों में भूस्खलन क े  साथ उच्चतम स्थावनक संींि है। ढलान ीनाने वालब सामग्रब क े  उद्देश्य क्षेत्र क े अध्ययन क े  ीाद, कमजोर िट्टान
और ढबले मलीे को उच्चतम सकारात्मक मूल्य पाया र्या है और भूस्खलन शुरू करने की अविक संभावना है और अविकतम लैंडस्लाइड
घटना फवौरावीवलटब स्कोर मान असाइन ककया र्या है।

मानवित्र संभाववत भूस्खलन िेत्रो को पहिानने में अत्यविक सहायक है ,और इसवलए वसववल संरिनाओं क े वनमागण क े दौरान और
उसक े  दौरान ढलानों की क्षेत्रबय सापेक्ष वस्थरता का मूल्यांकन करने में अत्यविक सहायता का हो सकता है।

The authors carried out landslide susceptibility mapping during the Field Season
2017-2018, covering an area of approx. 1 391 km2, on macro -Scale (1:50,000) in parts of
Toposheets 78 O/6 &78 O /7 parts of East Khasi Hills, South West Khasi Hills Districts,
Meghalaya. The objective is to prepare landslide susceptibility map using heuristic method
and multi-class index overlay technique on GIS platform and classify the area into varying
degree of landslide prone zones. This is achieved by preparing landslide inventory database
and also preparing Toposheet -wise spatial database for relevant geo -factors or thematic
maps using high resolution remote sensing techniques and field inputs. Analytical
Hierarchy Process is employed for mutual pair -wise comparison of factor classes. The
ratings for the factor classes have been assigned based on objective knowledge, discussion
and re-assessment through field inputs. A total six geo -factors viz. slope angle, curvature,
land use and land cover (LULC), geomorphology, slope forming material (SF M) and
regolith thickness maps were used as input thematic maps. The maps were integrated in
GIS using weighted multiclass index overlay method to obtain the susceptibility score map,
which was finally classified into ‘high’, ‘moderate’ and ‘low’ based on the break values
logically obtained by classifying the overall ratings of factor classes in relation to their
Altogether, 25 landslides have been documented following 42-point proforma out
of which 2 2 are debris slid es, 3 are rock slides and 1 earth flow.  In addition, a bout 27
natural landslides were identified through google earth imagery. Field observations and
documentation of existing landslides show that they are triggered largely by rain during
monsoon season.  Further, significant anthropogenic interference through modification of
slope profile has been found to be a major causative factor for inducing local instability.
Amongst the six geo -factor themes considered in the study, the slope and LULC carry an
integer weight of 13 and 9 respectively and have maximum control in spatial distribution of
landslides. In slope factor, 25°-35° classes have the maximum Landslide Occurrence
Favourability Score values while in land use and land cover, the extensive slope cut an d
quarry sections along the road corridors have the highest Landslide Occurrence
Favourability Score values. Amongst the geomorphology factor classes, denudational hills
and highly dissected slopes have highest spatial relation with landslides. After objec tive
field studies of slope forming material, the weathered rock and loose debris have been
found to have the highest positive value and are more likely to initiate landslide and have
been assigned the maximum Landslide Occurrence Favourability Score values.
The current study shows that only 0.67 % of the total area is under highly
susceptible area while moderately susceptible area accounts for 10.06% and low susceptible
area for 89.27%. The susceptibility map is the outcome of both  remote sensing and field
inputs and the map shows qualitative estimate of landslide susceptibility of the study area in
1:50,000 and is regional in application. The map can be of immense help in identifying the
potential landslide prone areas to zero down on specific locations of  interest and therefore

The state of Meghalaya receives very high amount of monsoon rainfall for about five
months (June -October) every year which act as a vital triggering  factor for landslides.
Moreover, the state is located in a region highly prone to earthquakes of moderate to high/very
high magnitude (Zone- V; BIS 2002) , which also act as  another potential triggering factor.
There are neo-tectonically active faults with historical seismic event such as 1897 Shillong
Earthquake. In the event of a shallow focus or higher magnitude earthquake, the propensity
for large scale initiation of earthquake-induced landslides is high.
The region has seen rapid development in infra-structure and communication in the
recent years. District headquarters Nongstoin of West Khasi Hills district, Mawkyrwat of
South-West Khasi Hills district and its adjacent areas have experienced rapid urbanization.
Expeditious developmental activities have been observed along several adjoining villages
in terms of road construction and public utility grounds in which slope modification has
been invariably involved. Exploitation of resources in terms of sand mining and rock
quarrying along the hillslopes has also caused i nitiation of slope failures . This is a major
concern in the vicinity of the settlement and along communication corridors particularly
NH-44E which connects Shillong, Nongstoin, Tura  and Mawkyrwat-Shnongkalong etc.,
and other significant tourist places within the state.
The NLSM programme has the following objectives: (i) Categorisation of the
hillslopes in terms of landslide susceptibility based on Analytical Hierarchical Process
using multi -class Index Overlay method  (ii) Preparation of landslide inventory database
using high resolution remote sensing data, archival information and field inputs  (iii)
Preparation of spatial database for geofactors of landslides.
The methodology employed is a GIS -based approach, through deve lopment of
terrain-specific weights/ ratings systems and a simple knowledge -driven technique -Multi-
class Index Overlay method of data integration to finally arrive at the 1:50,000 scale
landslide susceptibility maps . Th e current item code for FSP 2017 -18 is
M4LSSM/NC/NER/ SU -MEG/2017/12672 and the study covers about ≈1391km2 of two

A reconnitory field traverse was carried out in parts of TS 78 O/6 from July 13 th
2017 to get perspective understanding of t he geology, SFM and landuse pattern.  The field
traverse helped identify the predisposing factors and slope stability condition in the area.
The traverses were undertaken with the objective  to understand the anatomy and different
attributes of the landslide s as per the recommended 41 point geo -parametric landslide
inventory.Initially parts of TS No 78O/6 were completed after which field checks were
carried out for TS No 78O/7. The objective of the traverses was to update and validate the
pre-field maps of parts the three Toposheets. The earlier ratings of factor classes and inter -
predictor weights tentatively fixed were re -assessed and necessary changes were made as
per the inputs from field observations.

In the study area the gentle rolling topography is a result of differential weathering
of the gneissic, granitic rocks and sandstones . The gneissic and granitic lithology in the
central and south eastern part of TS no.78O/06 and the northern and north -eastern part of
TS no.78O/07 have rolling topography. However in the northern part of TS no.78O/06 and
southern parts of TS no. 78O/07, dominated by  basement rock overlain by  Mahadek
sandstones (Khasi group), have rugged and steep topography. The highest elevation is 1790
m near Rambrai Village (25˚38΄00΄΄, 91˚21΄00 ΄΄) in TS 78O/06 whereas the lowest
elevation is 80m above MSL along Um Ngi river section (25˚24΄00΄΄, 91˚15΄00΄΄) in the
southern part of the area  bordering Bangladesh in TS 78O/07. The general slope trend is
generally southerly  in the study area . The prominent linear depressions and low ridges

Geologically, Meghalaya comprises rocks ranging from the oldest Pre -cambrian
Gneissic complex to the recent alluvium formations. The Gneissic Complex which
represents the basement rock is overlain by the Shillong Group of rocks comprising mainly
of quartzites. They are intruded by basic and ultrabasic intrusives and also by gran ite
plutons. The Sylhet Trap in Meghalaya is found in a narrow E -W strip in the southern
fringe of the state. The Cretaceous and Tertiary sediments are found mostly in the southern
borders of the Khasi and Jaintia Hills and in western parts in Garo  Hills (Geology and
Mineral resources of Meghalaya, GSI Misc. Pub. 30 Pt. 4 Vol. 2 (ii)).
Geologically, the major area of TS 78O/06 & 07 exposes rock of Assam Meghalaya
Gneissic Complex and granite represented by Myliem and South Khasi Batholith belonging
to Archaen to Proterozoic age. The river sections and linear depressions also expose
basement rock. A thick cover of sedimentary sequence of KhasiGroup overlies the
basement rock in the south covering the larger area of the southern part of TS 78O/07. The
Khasi Group in the  study area is represented predominantly by  Mahadek Formation
comprising of arkosic gritty sandstone . Parts of TS 78O/07 area have minor patches of
Jaintia Group represented by gritty sandstone, shale, siltstone, Clay & coal.

Bangladesh Plains in th e south. It is bounded by the E -W trending Brahmaputra fault
systems in the north and the Dauki fault systems in the south  which separates the plateau

Meghalaya is a tribal state and the l and use and land cover pattern in Meghalaya is
influenced by social, cultural and economic needs of the people. The land use in the state is
intricately linked to traditional practices and needs since time immemorial. This influence
is given effect both by individual endeavour or collective community decision such as
farming collectively in large tract of land. Of late, the development activities by several
government setups have had significant impact on the land use and land cover pattern.
The people practice jhum as well as terrace cultivation besides consistent ly making
use of available space as homestead farming. The geo-climatic environment of Meghalaya
offers an excellent scope for  growing of different types of h orticultural crops including
fruits, vegetables, spices, and plantation crops, medicinal and aroma tic plants of high
economic values.  Spices such as black pepper, turmeric, ginger and chil lies are grown
abundantly on the slopes . Since time immemorial, arecanut , Areca catechu , has been
grown in Meghalaya as an important cash crop.
The people practice terrace cultivation in the valleys and foot slopes and to achieve
this water canals are being used for irrigation . The canals are mostly unlined and cut along
the slopes. The low lying areas between the gently undulating hills are invariably  dug as
ponds/reservoir to impound the runoff water as water easily accumulates in these areas.
The vegetation cover over the gently undulating hill mounds in southern plateau top
includes grass and shrubs. A wide variety of wild cultivable plants, edible fruits, leafy
vegetables and orchids are found in the natural habitat. However , over exploitation,
deforestation and habitat destruction has threatened this varied species and are now mainly
confined to the protected forest and groves maintained by the community.

Landslide susceptibility map represents areas or slopes most likely to fail in response
to various geo-environmental factors. The combination of pre-disposing and triggering factors
determines the spatial distribution of landslides. Therefore, the susceptibility analysis calls for
understanding the intricate relationship of causative geo -environmental factors with
landslides. A susceptibility map will therefore give qualitative or quantitative estimation of
how the mapping unit (e.g., a pixel, slope unit orfacet) will be susceptible to a potential
However, it may be categorically mentioned that the future landslide does not refer to
any specific time frame or frequency of occurrence nor does it carry any connotation on the
magnitude or scale of the failure. It is merely an establishment of relationship of relevant geo-
environmental causative factors with landslides for the areas of interest and based on which a
qualitative assessment can be reached with regard to their stability.
In the current study individual rating for geo-factor classes and weights of geo-factors
have been determined using Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) after preparing the pairwise
qualitative comparison matrix of all factors ( Saaty, 1977) after due discussion among the
The most relevant underlying factors in the initiation of landslides have been taken
into account in the area as it is deficient of landslides for which t he AHP has been adopted.
This caters to the needs of the terrain specific condition and therefore apriori knowledge or
reasonable assumption of the main causes of landslides in the area of interest is essential in
selecting t he most r elevant f actors out of the ma ny kn own p reparatory fa ctors that can
“theoretically” cause landslides (Ghosh and Carranza, 2010). Such preparatory factors for
landslide susceptibility analysis d epends on the s cale of analysis, the characteristics of the
study area, t he landslide type, the f ailure me chanisms and deductive knowledge of the
main causes of landslid es ( Guzzetti et al, 1999; Glade and Crozier, 2005). A systematic
overview of the i mportant p reparatory fa ctors required for susc eptibility mapping in
different scales is given in Van Westen et al, (2008).
None of the geo factors mentioned in the methodology  (1.7) can be singularly
attributed for the initiation of slope failures because it is the combination of various geo -
environmental factors that act to initiate landslides in any given slope. These include both pre-
disposing and triggering factors. However, these factors have varying degree of influence on
slope stability. While some factor is more important than others in any given place there is
change in various parameters from one place to another. In other words, the influence of the
geo-factors will have spatial variation. In addition to this, there can be temporal variation as
most landslides are triggered by heavy downpour during monsoon which is the case in
Meghalaya. For each theme the possible factor classes are considered for preparation of geo-
factor databases for the GIS-based analysis of susceptibility to landsliding. Landslides occur
when the shearing stress along the failure plane exceeds the shearing strength of rock/debris

same logic or concept used in assigni ng rating to the classes can  be used. In any pairwise

we assign rating ≤3 to any class (lower than 30% of the absolute difference value of 9), the

margin or weightage to determinethe break values between “Low” and “M oderate”

break value between moderate and high is placed at 0.5.
